transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because this has been going on for nearly two years now, and I know people keep telling me I’m making too much of it, but I’m not. It started with the kitchen work, the contractor, and then it became clear to me that it wasn’t just sloppy work or misunderstandings. He and some people on my block have been quietly working together, I’m sure of it, to cheat us and keep the kitchen half-wrong on purpose.

My husband keeps showing me receipts and saying, “See, this is what we paid for,” or “They explained that,” but receipts don’t prove people are honest. They can still make excuses, and that’s what they’ve been doing—excuse after excuse. And after this long, almost two years, you can’t tell me it’s all accidental. So that’s why I came in, because I need someone to understand what’s really been happening.
Do you believe these people can do things that ordinary people could not do, like control your thoughts or send you special messages?

No, not like controlling my thoughts or sending me secret messages, if that’s what you mean. It’s not some… supernatural thing. It’s very ordinary, actually, which is what makes it so upsetting. It’s people talking to each other, covering for each other, making excuses, acting like the kitchen was done properly when it wasn’t.

For nearly two years I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us, or at least to keep us from getting what we paid for. My husband keeps bringing out receipts like that settles it, but receipts don’t prove anyone acted honestly. They can write down whatever they want and still leave things half-wrong, then say, “Oh, that’s how it was supposed to be,” or “You misunderstood.” It’s not mind control. It’s just dishonest people being careful about it.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I hear normal things, like if someone’s talking outside or the television is on in another room, but not voices when nobody is there, not in that way.

Sometimes I do replay conversations in my head, you know, things the contractor said or things neighbors have said, and I go over it because the wording matters. People act like I’m just obsessing, but if someone says one thing and then later acts like they meant something else, you have to pay attention. But that’s me thinking about it, not hearing a voice out loud.

So no, I wouldn’t say I hear voices when no one is there.
Aside from this problem with the contractor and neighbors, has your day-to-day life stayed mostly normal?

Yes, mostly, I’d say. I mean, I’m not just sitting around doing nothing except thinking about the kitchen, if that’s what people imagine. I still go to my church gatherings, and I’m there when I say I’ll be there. I still go to book club — sometimes I have to make myself focus if there’s been some new nonsense with the remodel, but I go, I read the book, I talk with the ladies.

At home I keep up with the usual things, the laundry, meals, straightening up, the bills and appointments and all that. And with my family, we still make plans the way we always have — birthdays, dinners, visits, whatever is on the calendar. I don’t feel like my whole life has stopped.

It’s just that this contractor situation is sitting there in the middle of everything, and people act like because I can still do ordinary things, that means nothing is wrong. But I do keep my routines. I’ve tried very hard not to let them take that from me too.
Before all this started, had you developed any new medical or neurological illness?

I don’t think so. I mean, not that I’m aware of. Nobody sat me down and said, “You have some new neurological illness,” or anything like that.

I’m 67, so of course there are ordinary aches and things people get as they get older, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m twenty-five. But before all this with the contractor and the neighbors started, I can’t point to some big new medical problem that began and then everything changed after that. At least, nothing I recognized that way.

What do you mean exactly by neurological — like a stroke or seizures or something with the brain? Because no, not that I know of.
Before the kitchen problem began, did you generally tend to distrust other people’s motives?

I don’t know that I would put it that way. I mean, everybody has a little caution, don’t they? You don’t just believe every salesman or every person who smiles at you, especially by my age. You learn to notice when something doesn’t sound right.

But before the kitchen issue, I wouldn’t have said I walked around thinking people had bad motives all the time. I had normal relationships, normal dealings with people. If someone was polite and did what they said they were going to do, I didn’t sit there picking it apart.

So… no, not generally, I don’t think. Not as a personality thing. I was careful, maybe, but I don’t think I was distrustful of everyone.
Have other people told you that your speech or thoughts seem hard to follow or mixed up?

No, I don’t think anyone has said that to me. Not in those words anyway. People get impatient with me sometimes because I explain things fully, and maybe I go back over the details because I want them to understand the order of what happened, but that’s not the same as being mixed up.

My family might say, “Okay, Mom, we get it,” or “You already told us that part,” but I think that’s more because they don’t want to hear the whole thing again. I haven’t had anyone tell me I’m not making sense, or that they can’t follow my thoughts. I feel like I’m pretty clear when people actually listen.
During this time, have you had a period when you felt unusually high or depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I’d say “unusually high,” no. I mean, I’ve had days where I felt more worked up or on edge, especially when I was thinking about what was happening, but that’s not the same as feeling high, like euphoric or full of energy for no reason. I don’t think I’ve had anything like that.

Depressed… I don’t know. I’ve been upset, certainly. Anybody would be upset if they felt they weren’t being heard or things were going on around them that weren’t right. There were days I felt worn down by it, and I probably looked sad or tired to other people. But “depressed most of the day nearly every day” — I’m not sure. I wouldn’t want to say yes to that if it means something more specific than just being discouraged or frustrated.

So I guess my answer is no, not in that clear way you’re asking. More stressed and upset than unusually high or deeply depressed.
If someone showed you clear proof that the contractor had done the work exactly as agreed, would you be able to accept that?

Well… see, that’s the problem with saying “clear proof,” because everyone keeps acting like a receipt or a piece of paper settles the whole thing. My husband has shown me receipts, and I’ve looked at them, I really have. I’m not just refusing to look. But a receipt doesn’t prove what was actually agreed in the kitchen, or what was done on purpose, or who was talking to who afterward.

If someone could truly show me, not just wave papers at me, but truly show me that everything was done exactly the way it was supposed to be, I’d want to be fair. I’m not trying to be impossible. But I’ve been living with this for nearly two years, and the way the contractor handled it, and then the way certain people on the block seemed to know things or act like they were part of it… it’s hard to just erase all that because someone says, “Here, look, proof.”

So I don’t know. I suppose I’d look at it. But honestly, I think I’d still wonder what wasn’t being shown to me. Because from where I’m standing, it has felt very much like they’ve been working together to cheat us and leave things half-wrong on purpose, and the explanations just don’t cover that.
Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about the contractor and neighbors working together against you?

I mean… possible in the way that anything is possible, I suppose. I’m not trying to say I’m perfect or that I’ve never misunderstood something in my life. But with this, no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken.

It’s been nearly two years of this kitchen being left half-wrong, and every time I bring it up, there’s another excuse or another receipt or someone telling me I’m making too much of it. But the papers my husband shows me don’t explain the way the contractor acted, or the things people on the block seemed to know, or the feeling that they were all sort of quietly on the same side, if that makes sense.

So if you’re asking whether I can sit here and say, “Yes, maybe I invented the whole thing,” then no, I can’t say that honestly. I feel very sure they’ve been working together to cheat us, or at least to keep me from getting the kitchen fixed the way it was supposed to be. And I know that sounds like I’m being stubborn, but when you’ve watched it happen piece by piece for this long, it doesn’t feel like a mistake.
Aside from the kitchen and the neighbors involved with it, do you believe anyone else is trying to harm, cheat, or conspire against you?

No, not really anyone outside of that. I mean, I don’t go around thinking the whole world is after me or anything like that. It’s specifically this situation with the kitchen — the contractor, and then some people on the block who seemed to know things or act like they were involved somehow.

That’s why it’s been so upsetting, because it’s not just that the kitchen was done wrong. It’s that for nearly two years now I’ve felt sure they’ve been quietly working together to cheat us, or to keep it half-wrong on purpose, and every time I try to point it out, there’s another excuse or somebody acts like I’m the one making trouble. My husband keeps showing me receipts, like that should end the whole conversation, but those don’t explain what actually happened or why it’s still not right.

But aside from that, no. I’m not saying strangers or the government or people at the store are conspiring against me. It’s this contractor and the neighbors connected with it. That’s where it is.
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, not in the way you mean, like seeing people or shapes or things that aren’t there. I’ve never had that, as far as I know.

Sometimes I notice things other people don’t notice, like someone looking over at our house or acting a certain way, but that’s different. That’s me noticing what’s going on, not seeing something invisible or… imaginary. So no, I wouldn’t say I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.
For how long have you been convinced that the contractor and some neighbors were working together against you?

It’s been about… I’d say about a year and nine months now. Close to that. It started when the kitchen and the garden remodeling began, when everything in the house got disrupted and torn up and nothing was put back the way it should’ve been.

At first I don’t know that I would have said, “They’re all working together,” right that minute. In the beginning I was just upset because the work was wrong and the house was a mess. But as the months went on, and things kept not being fixed, and people around us seemed to know bits of what was happening or act funny about it, that’s when I became convinced it wasn’t just poor work or a misunderstanding.

So, yes, roughly a year and nine months that I’ve felt sure there was something going on with the contractor and some of the neighbors. It feels like a long time to live with your own house not feeling settled.
Have you been having problems with your memory?

Memory? I don’t know… I mean, I’m 67, so sometimes I walk into a room and forget what I went in there for, or I have to think for a second where I put my glasses, but I don’t know that I’d call that a “problem” exactly. My husband might say I repeat myself sometimes, but I think that’s more because I’m trying to explain something and nobody is really listening the first time.

I haven’t noticed anything like getting lost or not knowing who people are, if that’s what you mean. I keep track of the usual things. I remember what happened with the house very clearly, probably too clearly, because it’s been weighing on me so much. But regular memory problems… no, not in any big way that I can point to.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being put into your mind by someone else?

No, not like that. I’ve never felt like somebody was putting thoughts into my head, like controlling my mind or planting words there. My thoughts are my own.

What I have felt — and this is why I’m here, really — is that for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been working together quietly against us. Not in my head, but in real life. Like they were cheating us, dragging things out, keeping the kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and then acting like we were the difficult ones.

And I know my husband keeps showing me receipts and saying, “Look, this is what was paid,” or “This is what they said,” and they always have some excuse, but it doesn’t add up to me. It hasn’t added up for a long time. So no, I don’t think thoughts are being put into my mind. It’s more that I can see what’s been happening and nobody wants to admit it.
Before this kitchen situation began, did the people close to you generally see you as a suspicious person?

Before all this? I don’t think so, no. I mean, people might have said I was careful, maybe particular about things, especially with the house or money or who we hired, but suspicious as a person? I wouldn’t have thought so.

I got along with people well enough. I wasn’t sitting around thinking neighbors were up to something or that everyone had bad intentions. If something seemed off, I’d ask questions, but that’s just being sensible, isn’t it? My husband sometimes says I can worry over details, but that’s different from being suspicious of people for no reason.

So, no… as far as I know, before the kitchen trouble started, I don’t think people close to me generally saw me that way. At least they never said that to me.
Over the past two years, have you become less able to manage things you used to handle easily, like finances, appointments, or cooking?

No, not really, aside from anything that has to do with the remodel. That whole thing takes up too much of my time and patience, I’ll admit that, and it can throw me off because I’m making calls or looking over papers or thinking about what still isn’t right. But regular life? I still manage that.

I still go to my church gatherings, and I keep up with book club — I mean, sometimes I’m not in the mood if I’ve been upset about the house, but I still go and I know what we’re reading and when we’re meeting. Around the house I do the usual routines, the laundry, meals, keeping things in order as much as anyone can. And with family plans, I’m still the one who remembers who’s coming when, birthdays, dinners, that kind of thing.

So I wouldn’t say I’ve become unable to manage things I used to handle. It’s more that the remodel has become this awful, tangled thing that demands attention. But outside of that, I’m keeping up the way I always have.
Has anyone close to you noticed that your memory or thinking has become worse over the last two years?

I don’t think so… not in any real way. My husband might say I repeat myself about the kitchen, but that’s because it’s still not settled, not because I can’t remember things. I remember what was said, I remember what was promised, and I remember when people changed their story — that’s part of why it bothers me so much.

As far as regular things, I haven’t had anyone sit me down and say, “Your memory is getting worse,” or anything like that. I don’t think my children have said that either. Sometimes I’ll misplace my glasses or walk into a room and forget what I went in for, but who doesn’t do that at my age? That doesn’t feel like some big change over the last two years.

Thinking-wise, I feel like I’m still following things. I manage conversations, I read for book club, I keep track of family plans. So no, I wouldn’t say anyone close to me has noticed that my memory or thinking has gone downhill. If anything, they just think I’m too focused on this one situation, but that’s different.
Did your certainty that the contractor and neighbors were working together against you come on suddenly, all at once?

No, I wouldn’t say it came all at once, like waking up one morning and suddenly deciding that. It was more… it built up. Little things kept happening with the kitchen, things not done right, things being delayed, explanations that didn’t match what we were told before. And then certain neighbors seemed to know things or act strangely around it, and after a while it was very hard not to see the connection.

For nearly two years now, I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep the kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband keeps showing me receipts and saying, “See, this was paid for,” or “They said it was a supply issue,” but receipts don’t explain everything. People can have paperwork and still be dishonest. And the excuses just kept piling up.

So, no, not suddenly exactly. It became clearer over time, until I couldn’t really ignore it anymore.
Have you heard voices speaking to you or about you on more than a few occasions during this time?

No… I don’t think so. I mean, I hear people talking the normal way, of course — neighbors outside, people in the store, things like that — and sometimes I wonder what they’re saying if they lower their voices, especially if it seems like they stop when I come near. But I wouldn’t say I’ve heard voices speaking to me when no one was there, or voices talking about me out of nowhere.

There have been times I’ve thought people were discussing the house or the contractor business, but that’s more from how they act or the timing of things, not like a voice in my head or coming from the walls or anything. So no, not voices speaking to me on more than a few occasions. That’s not really how it’s been.

So I don’t know. I suppose I’d look at it. But honestly, I think I’d still wonder what wasn’t being shown to me. Because from where I’m standing, it has felt very much like they’ve been working together to cheat us and leave things half-wrong on purpose, and the explanations just don’t cover that.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the belief is a fixed delusion with little or no insight, which best distinguishes delusional disorder from paranoid personality traits and helps separate it from other psychotic disorders already less supported.
doctor.question: Do you think it is possible that you might be mistaken about the contractor and neighbors working together against you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about whether the belief about the contractor and neighbors conspiring could be mistaken, which assesses the fixed nature of the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I mean… possible in the way that anything is possible, I suppose. I’m not trying to say I’m perfect or that I’ve never misunderstood something in my life. But with this, no, I don’t really think I’m mistaken.

It’s been nearly two years of this kitchen being left half-wrong, and every time I bring it up, there’s another excuse or another receipt or someone telling me I’m making too much of it. But the papers my husband shows me don’t explain the way the contractor acted, or the things people on the block seemed to know, or the feeling that they were all sort of quietly on the same side, if that makes sense.

So if you’re asking whether I can sit here and say, “Yes, maybe I invented the whole thing,” then no, I can’t say that honestly. I feel very sure they’ve been working together to cheat us, or at least to keep me from getting the kitchen fixed the way it was supposed to be. And I know that sounds like I’m being stubborn, but when you’ve watched it happen piece by piece for this long, it doesn’t feel like a mistake.

doctor.intent: Differentiate persistent delusional disorder from acute/transient psychotic disorder, schizophrenia, and personality disorder by establishing whether the belief is circumscribed to this single topic or extends to other persecutory ideas.
doctor.question: Aside from the kitchen and the neighbors involved with it, do you believe anyone else is trying to harm, cheat, or conspire against you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the extent and content of paranoid/conspiratorial beliefs, specifically whether the fixed belief about being cheated or conspired against extends beyond the contractor and neighbors.

patient.answer:
No, not really anyone outside of that. I mean, I don’t go around thinking the whole world is after me or anything like that. It’s specifically this situation with the kitchen — the contractor, and then some people on the block who seemed to know things or act like they were involved somehow.

That’s why it’s been so upsetting, because it’s not just that the kitchen was done wrong. It’s that for nearly two years now I’ve felt sure they’ve been quietly working together to cheat us, or to keep it half-wrong on purpose, and every time I try to point it out, there’s another excuse or somebody acts like I’m the one making trouble. My husband keeps showing me receipts, like that should end the whole conversation, but those don’t explain what actually happened or why it’s still not right.

But aside from that, no. I’m not saying strangers or the government or people at the store are conspiring against me. It’s this contractor and the neighbors connected with it. That’s where it is.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there are persistent non-bizarre hallucinations, which would distinguish delusional disorder from schizophrenia or organic psychosis.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The question asks about visual hallucinations (seeing things others cannot see), but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, functioning, impairment related to the delusion, and duration; it does not include hallucinations.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, not in the way you mean, like seeing people or shapes or things that aren’t there. I’ve never had that, as far as I know.

Sometimes I notice things other people don’t notice, like someone looking over at our house or acting a certain way, but that’s different. That’s me noticing what’s going on, not seeing something invisible or… imaginary. So no, I wouldn’t say I’ve seen things other people couldn’t see.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a sustained non-bizarre persecutory delusion for at least 3 months, which would favor delusional disorder over acute/transient psychosis or schizophrenia.
doctor.question: For how long have you been convinced that the contractor and some neighbors were working together against you?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about 1 year and 9 months, since the kitchen and garden remodeling started disrupting the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the belief about the contractor and neighbors working together against the patient has been present.

patient.answer:
It’s been about… I’d say about a year and nine months now. Close to that. It started when the kitchen and the garden remodeling began, when everything in the house got disrupted and torn up and nothing was put back the way it should’ve been.

At first I don’t know that I would have said, “They’re all working together,” right that minute. In the beginning I was just upset because the work was wrong and the house was a mess. But as the months went on, and things kept not being fixed, and people around us seemed to know bits of what was happening or act funny about it, that’s when I became convinced it wasn’t just poor work or a misunderstanding.

So, yes, roughly a year and nine months that I’ve felt sure there was something going on with the contractor and some of the neighbors. It feels like a long time to live with your own house not feeling settled.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is underlying cognitive decline suggesting an organic psychotic disorder rather than primary delusional disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: Have you been having problems with your memory?

target_item.reason: The doctor's question is about memory problems, but the provided symptom profiles do not include memory impairment or cognitive symptoms.

patient.answer:
Memory? I don’t know… I mean, I’m 67, so sometimes I walk into a room and forget what I went in there for, or I have to think for a second where I put my glasses, but I don’t know that I’d call that a “problem” exactly. My husband might say I repeat myself sometimes, but I think that’s more because I’m trying to explain something and nobody is really listening the first time.

I haven’t noticed anything like getting lost or not knowing who people are, if that’s what you mean. I keep track of the usual things. I remember what happened with the house very clearly, probably too clearly, because it’s been weighing on me so much. But regular memory problems… no, not in any big way that I can point to.

doctor.intent: Assess for Schneiderian first-rank/passivity experiences to distinguish schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis from delusional disorder/paranoid personality.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being put into your mind by someone else?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about a possible delusional belief involving thought insertion, which falls under delusions.

patient.answer:
No, not like that. I’ve never felt like somebody was putting thoughts into my head, like controlling my mind or planting words there. My thoughts are my own.

What I have felt — and this is why I’m here, really — is that for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been working together quietly against us. Not in my head, but in real life. Like they were cheating us, dragging things out, keeping the kitchen half-wrong on purpose, and then acting like we were the difficult ones.

And I know my husband keeps showing me receipts and saying, “Look, this is what was paid,” or “This is what they said,” and they always have some excuse, but it doesn’t add up to me. It hasn’t added up for a long time. So no, I don’t think thoughts are being put into my mind. It’s more that I can see what’s been happening and nobody wants to admit it.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there has been a change in overall personality or social/interpersonal style suggestive of a long-standing paranoid personality versus a later-onset delusional disorder or psychosis.
doctor.question: Before this kitchen situation began, did the people close to you generally see you as a suspicious person?

target_item.reason: The question asks about whether others viewed me as generally suspicious before the kitchen situation, which relates to premorbid personality or baseline suspiciousness. The provided symptom profiles only cover the current delusion, duration, functioning, and its impact, not prior personality traits.

patient.answer:
Before all this? I don’t think so, no. I mean, people might have said I was careful, maybe particular about things, especially with the house or money or who we hired, but suspicious as a person? I wouldn’t have thought so.

I got along with people well enough. I wasn’t sitting around thinking neighbors were up to something or that everyone had bad intentions. If something seemed off, I’d ask questions, but that’s just being sensible, isn’t it? My husband sometimes says I can worry over details, but that’s different from being suspicious of people for no reason.

So, no… as far as I know, before the kitchen trouble started, I don’t think people close to me generally saw me that way. At least they never said that to me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has been a chronic progressive decline in cognition or functioning suggesting an organic psychotic disorder rather than primary delusional disorder or schizophrenia-spectrum illness.
doctor.question: Over the past two years, have you become less able to manage things you used to handle easily, like finances, appointments, or cooking?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: Outside of dealing with the remodel, I still keep up with my church gatherings, book club, household routines, and family plans the way I usually do.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether her everyday functioning has declined in areas like finances, appointments, or cooking, which directly relates to whether functioning is generally preserved apart from the delusional issue.

patient.answer:
No, not really, aside from anything that has to do with the remodel. That whole thing takes up too much of my time and patience, I’ll admit that, and it can throw me off because I’m making calls or looking over papers or thinking about what still isn’t right. But regular life? I still manage that.

I still go to my church gatherings, and I keep up with book club — I mean, sometimes I’m not in the mood if I’ve been upset about the house, but I still go and I know what we’re reading and when we’re meeting. Around the house I do the usual routines, the laundry, meals, keeping things in order as much as anyone can. And with family plans, I’m still the one who remembers who’s coming when, birthdays, dinners, that kind of thing.

So I wouldn’t say I’ve become unable to manage things I used to handle. It’s more that the remodel has become this awful, tangled thing that demands attention. But outside of that, I’m keeping up the way I always have.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the fixed persecutory belief is occurring in the context of a neurocognitive syndrome, which would help distinguish an organic delusional disorder from primary delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Has anyone close to you noticed that your memory or thinking has become worse over the last two years?

target_item.reason: The question is asking about decline in memory or thinking over the last two years, but the provided symptom profile does not include cognitive impairment or memory problems.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… not in any real way. My husband might say I repeat myself about the kitchen, but that’s because it’s still not settled, not because I can’t remember things. I remember what was said, I remember what was promised, and I remember when people changed their story — that’s part of why it bothers me so much.

As far as regular things, I haven’t had anyone sit me down and say, “Your memory is getting worse,” or anything like that. I don’t think my children have said that either. Sometimes I’ll misplace my glasses or walk into a room and forget what I went in for, but who doesn’t do that at my age? That doesn’t feel like some big change over the last two years.

Thinking-wise, I feel like I’m still following things. I manage conversations, I read for book club, I keep track of family plans. So no, I wouldn’t say anyone close to me has noticed that my memory or thinking has gone downhill. If anything, they just think I’m too focused on this one situation, but that’s different.

doctor.intent: Differentiate delusional disorder from acute/transient psychotic disorder by confirming whether the belief developed gradually rather than suddenly.
doctor.question: Did your certainty that the contractor and neighbors were working together against you come on suddenly, all at once?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for nearly two years now I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep my kitchen half-wrong on purpose, no matter how many receipts my husband shows me or how many excuses they give.
target_item.reason: The question is directly about the patient's certainty that the contractor and neighbors were working together against her, which is the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
No, I wouldn’t say it came all at once, like waking up one morning and suddenly deciding that. It was more… it built up. Little things kept happening with the kitchen, things not done right, things being delayed, explanations that didn’t match what we were told before. And then certain neighbors seemed to know things or act strangely around it, and after a while it was very hard not to see the connection.

For nearly two years now, I’ve been sure the contractor and some people on my block have been quietly working together to cheat us and keep the kitchen half-wrong on purpose. My husband keeps showing me receipts and saying, “See, this was paid for,” or “They said it was a supply issue,” but receipts don’t explain everything. People can have paperwork and still be dishonest. And the excuses just kept piling up.

So, no, not suddenly exactly. It became clearer over time, until I couldn’t really ignore it anymore.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are sustained hallucinations occurring with the delusion, which would help distinguish persistent delusional disorder from schizophrenia-like or acute psychotic disorders.
doctor.question: Have you heard voices speaking to you or about you on more than a few occasions during this time?

target_item.reason: The question is about hearing voices, i.e., auditory hallucinations, but the provided symptom profile only covers delusions, functioning, impairment related to the delusion, and duration.

patient.answer:
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I hear people talking the normal way, of course — neighbors outside, people in the store, things like that — and sometimes I wonder what they’re saying if they lower their voices, especially if it seems like they stop when I come near. But I wouldn’t say I’ve heard voices speaking to me when no one was there, or voices talking about me out of nowhere.

There have been times I’ve thought people were discussing the house or the contractor business, but that’s more from how they act or the timing of things, not like a voice in my head or coming from the walls or anything. So no, not voices speaking to me on more than a few occasions. That’s not really how it’s been.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main concern in their own words to guide the diagnostic interview
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusional belief that a contractor and some neighbors have conspired to cheat her, lasting about 1 year and 9 months. She remains firmly convinced despite contrary evidence, yet does not report hallucinations, thought insertion/control, disorganized speech, prominent mood episodes, cognitive decline, or broad functional deterioration. The delusion is circumscribed rather than pervasive as a longstanding personality style, and there is no evidence of a medical/neurological cause or acute polymorphic onset. This most strongly supports persistent delusional disorder.
